abstract: We study last-iterate learning of mixed Nash equilibria in atomic symmetric congestion games under resource semi-bandit feedback, where players observe both the costs and the loads of their selected resources. For strictly increasing latency functions, the restriction of the potential function to symmetric marginal profiles is strongly convex. However, players' independent stochastic updates need not preserve this symmetry without explicit synchronization. We show that a quadratic consensus penalty makes the potential globally strongly convex while making the symmetric equilibrium the unique minimizer of the transformed potential. We propose a variant of online projected gradient descent that achieves $O(t^{-2/3})$ squared distance to equilibrium and $O(t^{-1/3})$ maximum deviation gain in expectation, for every $t\geq 1$ and for any initialization. The played profile also converges to equilibrium almost surely.
